articles.title: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency
articles.read_scope: Complete main prose, Planning for failure through Codifying the design of robust APIs; examples inspected, not copied.

practice.trigger: Retrying a mutating operation after an uncertain network outcome.
practice.failure: The effect succeeds but its response disappears; another attempt repeats the effect.
practice.mechanism: Preserve one operation identity and recover or replay its durable outcome; apply bounded backoff with jitter.
practice.conditions: The downstream contract must actually support the identity and recovery horizon.
practice.counterexample: Generating a fresh key after a timeout creates a distinct operation.
practice.verification: Force response loss after the effect; retry with the original identity and assert one business effect.

articles.limitations: Historical introduction; current API docs refine retention, saved failures, and pre-execution conflicts.

articles.title: Under Deconstruction: The State of Shopify’s Monolith
articles.read_scope: Complete main prose from introduction through What We’re Building Right Now, acknowledgments, and further-reading list; captions inspected.

practice.trigger: A boundary refactor still makes ordinary changes span many components.
practice.failure: New interfaces preserve dependency cycles and scatter cohesive behavior.
practice.mechanism: Inspect dependency direction and actual co-changing behavior together; move responsibilities and enforce useful contracts incrementally.
practice.conditions: Choose the intermediate state for the real ownership or isolation goal.
practice.counterexample: A uniform wrapper around every module adds indirection without independence.
practice.verification: Trace representative changes, measure affected components, and reject newly forbidden dependencies.

articles.limitations: Rails-specific historical tools are examples, not recommended defaults for Python, TypeScript, or Go.

articles.title: Automating MySQL schema migrations with GitHub Actions and more
articles.read_scope: Complete main prose, process, schema-diff examples, numbered orchestration flow, analysis, and public-availability limitations.

practice.trigger: A schema migration spans review, long execution, cut-over, and cleanup.
practice.failure: Manual tracking loses status, dependencies, and responsibility across those transitions.
practice.mechanism: Version schema intent, compute executable changes in isolation, and persist orchestration state with explicit owners and resource scheduling.
practice.conditions: Verify actual engine, topology, tooling constraints, and migration authority.
practice.counterexample: A textual schema diff or successful copy does not prove safe cut-over.
practice.verification: Exercise pause, failed cut-over, restart, completion accounting, and client compatibility.

articles.limitations: Historical internal controller is not turnkey software; current gh-ost docs explicitly describe brief cut-over blocking.

articles.title: How Uber Protects Against Retry Storms
articles.read_scope: Complete main prose and tables, including correlation limitations, absent retries, context loss, production account, and conclusion; diagram captions inspected.

practice.trigger: Several service layers retry the same downstream failure.
practice.failure: Locally reasonable budgets multiply traffic along the dependency chain.
practice.mechanism: Identify error origin and retry ownership across hops; propagate sufficient context to suppress redundant upstream retries.
practice.conditions: Validate correlation, missing context, and whether an eligible retry already occurred.
practice.counterexample: Blind suppression can remove the only recovery attempt or misclassify coincidental failures.
practice.verification: Inject one downstream failure and context loss; count attempts per hop and check recovery opportunities.

articles.limitations: Company-specific shared infrastructure; reported improvements are not universal guarantees or repository measurements.

runtime_crosschecks.finding: Executed first results include 500 responses; validation and concurrent-request conflicts before execution are not saved. Keys may be pruned after at least 24 hours; reuse after pruning creates a new request. Payload mismatch is rejected.
runtime_crosschecks.implication: Reuse the existing idempotency contract reference rather than duplicating it in each language skill. Retained uncertainty needs reconciliation, not a new key.

runtime_crosschecks.finding: The documented atomic cut-over uses blocking locks and briefly blocks pending connections. Failure returns to the original-table phase for another attempt.
runtime_crosschecks.implication: Describe online migration as bounded operational impact, not literally lock-free. Test cut-over and lock acquisition with the deployed version.

runtime_crosschecks.finding: Transparent retries exist without a configured retry policy; configured retries depend on status, attempt limit, and backoff. Receiving response headers commits the RPC for the transport retry mechanism.
runtime_crosschecks.implication: Inventory SDK and transport retries alongside application retries. Transport commitment does not mean an external business effect committed.
